chunks: From him, from Fudayla, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi and Abu Basir and Abu al-Abbas, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
"He inherits her, and she does not inherit him, when the waiting period (iddah) has expired."

key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: The waiting period (iddah) after divorce or death
key_terms.تَرِثُهُ: He inherits her (the husband inheriting from the wife)

ai.seo_question: Does a divorced wife inherit from her ex-husband after the iddah expires?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the timing of inheritance rights in cases of *talaq* (divorce), specifying that the husband inherits from his wife only after the completion of the *iddah* (waiting period), while the wife does not inherit from him. This ruling is derived from the principle that the marital bond remains intact during *iddah*, making the husband an heir, whereas the wife's inheritance right from the husband is suspended until the divorce is finalized. The narration, transmitted through prominent companions like Abu Basir and Aban ibn Uthman, underscores the precise legal mechanics of marital dissolution in Shia jurisprudence.
